However, many upstream products continued to be imported from China or Chinese-controlled companies, causing continued investigations and duties on products entering the United States from new areas. These measures included AD/CVD investigations in 2021 and 2024 (which continued through new or existing investigations in 2025) on Chinese companies, or companies that relied on the low-cost Chinese supply chain, operating in Southeast Asia. In 2025, these investigations expanded to India. Measures also included the Hoshine withhold release order in June 2021 and UFLPA in June 2022, both of which aimed to stop importation of products that could contain material made using forced labor in Xinjiang, where much of China’s metallurgical-grade silicon (mg-Si) and solar-grade polysilicon is produced. In the past several years, the U.S. government enacted legislation providing tax credits, loans, and grants to PV module, component, and subcomponent manufacturing as well as PV inverter, PV tracker component, and BESS and component manufacturing. Among other goals, these incentives aimed to help U.S. products compete with imported products. Technologies with relatively small market shares in 2024 are not covered in the report, such as III-V, perovskite, copper-indium-gallium-diselenide (CIGS), and organic PV technologies. 5 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 2 Crystalline-Silicon Modules 2.1 Overview In 2024, U.S. demand for crystalline-silicon (c-Si) PV modules was increasingly met by modules manufactured in the United States, driven by the trends discussed in Section 1. The United States imported 45.9 GW of c-Si modules in 2024, which was only 0.4 GW more than in 2023 but dc dc up 100% from 2022. In 2024, 89% of c-Si modules imported into the United States came from Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia, Malaysia, and the remaining countries within the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)—up from 77% in 2023 (Feldman, Zuboy, Dummit, Stright, et al. 2025).6 However, module imports in the fourth quarter (Q4) of 2024 were 52% lower than quarterly average imports during Q1–Q3 2024, coinciding with growth in U.S. module production.
